item.description: - **Errors that say what to do.** Not logged in to Claude Code, out of usage, network or server trouble: the panel says which in plain words and offers Try Again. - **Chat history.** Finished chats stay on this Mac and can be read again from the clock button. They're read-only, private windows are never recorded, typed text and address data are trimmed before saving, and you can turn it off in Settings › AI. - **Better answers.** Code blocks, lists and tables render properly, with copy buttons. Links show where they really go, and after a chat has read other sites, opening a link asks first. Long tasks fold into "N steps" with a summary of the tabs opened and closed, and tabs the AI closed can be reopened. - **Easier to drive.** The tab the AI sees shows as a chip; type @ to attach another. ⌘E jumps to the panel, Esc stops, ↑ brings back your last message. Drag the panel's edge to resize it, pick the model from the chip under the box, get suggestions that fit the page, and choose Ask AI About Selection from a page's context menu. - **Questions in the panel.** The AI's questions appear as cards above the box instead of covering the window: Return or Esc says no, ⌘Return allows once, ⌥⌘Return allows that site for the chat. Allow keys only work inside the panel and after a short pause. Paying, deleting and signing in still ask in a window sheet. The panel's head shows which sites the chat has read, and you can take back a site you allowed. - **Images.** Attach a screenshot of the page, or drop or paste up to four images; they're resized and stripped of location data. Images count as something the AI read, so what it does next is asked about.
- **An even address bar.** There was more room above the address bar than below it. It now has the same space on both sides, the bar is a little shorter, and the window buttons sit level with it.

- **The page reaches the edges of the window.** The page used to sit on a card with a gap above, below and to the right of it, which showed as an empty band, most of all on a tall screen. It now runs to the window's top, bottom and right edge, and the AI panel does too, with a thin line between them. With the sidebar hidden or in focus mode, the page fills the whole window.

- **Translation works with the languages you downloaded.** Changmun asked you to download a language even after you had: macOS has a fast and a high-quality translation engine, and Changmun only looked for the fast one. It now uses whichever you have. Text it can't translate stays as it was instead of stopping the whole page, and if nothing could be translated, it says so instead of doing nothing. - **A headless Changmun for your agents.** `changmun headless start` runs a separate, invisible Changmun with its own empty profile, and `changmun --headless …` or `changmun --mcp --headless` (for Claude Code) points at it. It doesn't stop to ask before each step, so it refuses anything that can't be undone, like paying, sending, posting or deleting. Your own browser, its logins and its passwords stay out of it. See `changmun help`.

- **Changmun tells you whether its AI can run.** The last step of onboarding, and the AI panel until you first use it, now say whether Claude Code is on this Mac. If it isn't, you get a link to it, and a note that you can point Changmun at a copy it didn't find in Settings › AI. Codex, Gemini CLI and opencode are named as coming when they're what your Mac has. Until Claude Code is there, the panel's composer stays off instead of failing when you press Return. - **Fewer "Allow" questions from Claude Code.** An AI connected through MCP, such as a Claude Code session, can now be allowed on a site for the rest of its session, as the AI panel could already. It still asks again after reading another site, and anything that pays, sends, posts or deletes is still asked about every time. Commands from the command line are still asked each time.

- **Changmun updates itself.** New versions now arrive inside the app. Changmun looks for one once a day and asks before installing it; choose Changmun › Check for Updates… to look right away, or let it download and install updates on its own in Settings › Advanced. Every update is signed by the developer, and Changmun refuses one that isn't. This is the last version you need to install by hand, so the sidebar's brew note is gone. Homebrew keeps working and now knows that Changmun keeps itself up to date.
